title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Permissive Withdrawal - Timing
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A client has failed to pay their retainer replenishment despite several written reminders. The paralegal decides to withdraw. The trial is scheduled to begin in two days. According to the Rules of Conduct, can the paralegal withdraw at this time?
options: Yes, non-payment of fees is an absolute right to withdraw immediately.
No, permissive withdrawal for non-payment requires the paralegal to give reasonable notice, and withdrawing two days before trial would cause serious prejudice to the client.
Yes, provided the paralegal returns the client's original documents before the trial.
No, paralegals cannot withdraw for financial reasons under any circumstances once litigation has commenced.
questions.explain: Rule 8.02 governing optional withdrawal allows withdrawal for non-payment of fees, but the paralegal must give reasonable notice to the client. The withdrawal must not happen if it would result in serious prejudice to the client (e.g., right before a trial where they cannot reasonably find substitute representation).
